hero.headline: North Palm Beach Celebrates Fourth of July with Fireworks and America 250 Events
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk social media post
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board filed a court challenge Thursday against an administrative law judge's recommendation to reinstate a Spectrum Academy teacher who.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, sparked controversy with his comments labeling Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. According to an investigation report obtained by WPTV, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The judge recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. The school board still has final authority on whether Theobald gets his job back, and it's unclear when a final decision will be made.

cards.headline: DeSantis Allies Accuse Lieutenant Governor's Wife of Running Burner Accounts Critical of Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts were deactivated after prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team alleged they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations emerged that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both pointed to online research connecting the accounts to the Second Lady. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to a known number and email used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw said the content of the accounts suggested they existed entirely to advance Jay Collins' political ambitions as he runs for Governor. Redfern confirmed the FSUdude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern leveled their criticisms publicly. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit will have two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county as hundreds of boaters hit the waterw.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are expected on Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend. The Martin County Maritime Response Unit will deploy two boats with medics on standby in the north and south parts of the county to respond to emergencies. Lt. Brett Harry said the team is prepared to handle incidents ranging from minor injuries like stubbed toes to serious medical events including cardiac emergencies and potential spinal injuries.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, prioritizing safety on the water. Lt. Harry encouraged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd Seeks to Block Paula Stark From House District 47 Ballot After Filing Failure
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking a Leon Circuit Court to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork before the June 12 qualifying deadline. Stark filed her qualifying materials less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline, which state officials say prevented her from discovering a critical missing document. Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests required for all candidates, was never submitted by her treasurer and partner, Joel Davis.

Five state employees provided sworn written declarations stating that Davis never submitted Form 6 and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted other paperwork during the final hour of the qualifying window. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said in a court filing that three weeks after the deadline, Stark still has not submitted Form 6. According to Reeve, Stark was one of 12 candidates who failed to properly turn in the form, though half of them corrected the problems and qualified. Byrd argued that Stark and Davis knew Form 6 was required and could have discovered the missing document if they had not waited until the final hour to file their materials.

Reeve also documented a pattern of filing problems with Stark's campaign. The campaign has filed finance reports more than a month late, reported excessive contributions, and maintained an incorrect address on file. Audits in 2022 and 2024 found inconsistent transfers between campaign and office accounts. Additionally, a late report fine upheld by the Florida Elections Commission was referred to debt collection for nonpayment in November 2025. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November due to over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines.

If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 would be open to all voters to decide between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republicans filed to run in the traditionally blue House District representing Osceola and Orange counties. Byrd emphasized the time constraints involved in the decision, noting that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4, with vote-by-mail ballots due out between July 9 and 16. The Secretary of State argued that reversing course would be costly and likely risk confusion in the results of this race and others on the ballot.

cards.headline: Juno Beach considers thousands in costs to replace fence at JB-7 beach access after resident complaints
cards.teaser: Colony Condos residents say beachgoers have been cutting through their private property since the town removed a fence at the JB-7 public walkway in 2023, leading to confrontations and police calls.
cards.body:
A dispute over a missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is now a budget question for the town, with potential costs running into thousands of dollars. The fence at the JB-7 public walkway was removed in 2023 for safety reasons, but residents at the adjacent Colony Condos say the removal has created significant problems. Without the barrier, only bushes now separate the public access path from private property, leading to what residents describe as regular trespassing during the summer months.

Lori Hill, a Colony resident, explained that the lack of a clear boundary has resulted in beachgoers parking in condo spots and cutting through landscaping to access the beach with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Hill said the problem intensifies during summer season and has led to confrontations between residents and trespassers that sometimes turn hostile. Rather than continuing to engage in these disputes, residents have begun calling police to handle the situation. Hill expressed hope that the town would reinstall the fence to restore the clear property line and protect the condo's private parking and landscaping.

Not all beachgoers agree there is a major problem. Michael House, who regularly walks to JB-7 from a nearby public parking lot, said he has never witnessed the trespassing issues residents describe. House noted there is plenty of free parking available in the area and suggested that property damage or littering would be more significant concerns than the current access situation.

When the matter came before the Juno Beach Town Council, officials noted the town has no obligation to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested the town might explore lower-cost alternatives rather than a full fence replacement. Halpern proposed a combination approach using split rail fencing and shrubs to help residents while controlling expenses, acknowledging that traditional fencing carries a significant price tag. The council agreed to address the fence question as part of its budget discussions scheduled for July 15. The decision on whether to reinstall a fence and which solution to pursue will ultimately depend on available funds and council priorities during the budget deliberations.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities nationwide to receive the prestigious National Civic League honor, recognizing efforts to strengthen community engagement and civic participation.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach is celebrating after being named one of just 10 communities in the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League. Riviera Beach was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where Riviera Beach leaders presented the city's efforts to strengthen community engagement. Mayor Douglas Lawson called the recognition a proud moment, saying the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars," Lawson said.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several programs designed to increase civic participation, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy, the Citizens Leadership Academy with a 98 percent completion rate, and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson said the award is a tribute to the heart and determination of residents and that winning this brings back community pride. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state with record graduation rate
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 84 percent of district-operated schools rated A or B and a record 93.5 percent graduation rate.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County received an "A" rating from the state for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. School districts and schools receive letter grades from the Florida Department of Education based on factors including student performance on state tests, graduation rates and student performance on advanced coursework. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84 percent, were rated "A" or "B," up from 120 schools the previous year. The district set a record 93.5 percent graduation rate, with 86 percent of seniors participating in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education or Dual Enrollment courses. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a "C" rating last year to an "A" this year under the leadership of Principal Rona Tata, who has spent 15 years as principal after serving five years as assistant principal. The school had an "A" rating two years ago before narrowly missing a "B" rating the previous year by just a few points. Staff modified the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" rating to an "A" this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Boca Raton Community High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march a full mile along the National Mall in Washington D.C. on July 4, representing the entire state of Florida at the prestigious parade.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event. Junior Lola Cabezas acknowledged the pressure of performing before millions of people watching nationwide, but expressed confidence the band will rise to the occasion. She explained the physical demands of marching band, noting that musicians must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound without hearing their steps in the music.

Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is laser-focused on nailing every detail, particularly the marching and timing, knowing everyone will see what the Boca High band is capable of. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed full confidence in her students to put their best foot forward and represent the country well. Senior Lily Schaffer called the opportunity amazing, saying it showcases how much the program has grown. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those who want to cheer on the band from home.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance claim denied by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield less than 24 hours before scheduled breast reconstruction surgery using GalaFlex mesh.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy with planned reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex is still considered investigational and there is no or not enough proof it improves health.

GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not approved for breast reconstruction, where it remains an off-label, investigational and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated the treatment's efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined. Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it gives her patients the least amount of complications compared to other options. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after Billington found a mechanism to make it happen. Last year, after investigative reporting, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem said the mesh does not meet the standards required for coverage by its medical policy without FDA approval. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4 percent this year
cards.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4 percent from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. The survey attributes the increase to inflation. Ground beef prices are up 5.5 percent, while buns have risen 7.7 percent. Strawberries, affected by a Florida frost, have seen the largest increase at 12.4 percent. Ice cream prices are up 5.3 percent.

Not all food items have become more expensive. Potato prices have declined this year, benefiting shoppers planning to make potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades offers competitive pricing. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends shopping strategically by comparing prices across stores to find the best deals for items on your grocery list. She emphasized that reducing food waste is critical for families managing costs, and that process starts with creating a meal plan.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire as investigators point to electrical cause
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed their belongings.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office indicate an electrical issue may have caused the blaze. The fire remains under investigation as authorities work to determine the exact cause of the fatal incident.

White's fiancé Mark is now rebuilding his life after losing both his partner and many of his belongings in the flames. Friends learned of White's death when Mark called to inform them of the tragedy. In response to the loss, people who knew the couple have launched a fundraiser to help Mark recover from the financial devastation caused by the fire. "It's completely a state of devastation," said Nina Fenn, who had been White's friend for eight years and spoke about the impact of losing her longtime companion.

Fenn described White as a devoted Christian woman with a generous spirit who found joy in gardening, caring for plants, and playing piano. Those who knew her remembered her as someone who was always willing to help others and showed genuine love for the people around her, particularly children. The pain of White's death is intensified by the timing, as her birthday falls on the Fourth of July, meaning she passed away just days before turning another year older.

The tragedy is particularly difficult for Mark, who is grieving not only the loss of his fiancée but also carries the weight of previous heartbreak. Mark previously lost his only child, Jacob, in a tragic incident. Fenn emphasized her commitment to supporting Mark through this difficult period, acknowledging the compounding nature of his grief. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said, reflecting on how White's memory will remain with those who loved her.

cards.headline: Stuart's downtown dock closes Sunday for $3 million renovation that doubles slip capacity
cards.teaser: The dock will close July 6 for renovations projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. When finished, the project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels.
cards.body:
Stuart's downtown public dock will close July 6 for a $3 million renovation projected to be complete by next Fourth of July. The project will nearly double the dock's capacity, expanding from 18 to 44 slips for both motorized and non-motorized vessels. The renovation will include a 7,500 square foot fixed dock, a 1,400 square foot floating dock and a smaller floating platform. The project is funded by a state grant and transportation impact fees. Stuart Mayor Sean Reed said the upgrades address more than just capacity, as they are designed to prevent storm damage during hurricanes and major storms. With more than 1,400 boaters who use the dock annually, the improvements address current limitations.

During the closure, the city is working to accommodate businesses and boaters who rely on the dock. Tiki Taxi & Cruises, which operates off the dock, had initial concerns about continuing operations during construction. Austin Kuyrkendall, director of operations for Tiki Taxi & Cruises, said the city is allowing them to build a gate at the end of the downtown Stuart dock to board people during the renovation. Kuyrkendall said the dock plays a central role in Stuart's identity and economy, noting that crowding on busy weekends makes finding dock space difficult. He described the modernization project as a welcome change for both the city and his business.

cards.headline: Juno Beach condo residents demand town replace fence at JB-7 beach access point
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. A fix could cost the town thousands of dollars.
cards.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer when lots of cars park randomly and people push back bushes to cut through with their coolers, fishing rods and lawn chairs. Hill said residents remember when the fence made the boundary clear, and since it came down, confrontations with trespassers have become recurring. After getting rude responses when confronting people directly, residents have been calling police to handle the situation.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, suggesting the town could help residents with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs. Hill said residents are hopeful the town will act to restore the barrier so they can have their landscaping and private parking back. The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie approves land transfer for new Florida Turnpike interchange at Midway Road
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to FDOT to assist with a partial interchange. The city is also working on a $95 million road widening project along Midway Road.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange for the Florida Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between the entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. According to Samples, the interchange is about accessibility and accommodating growth that has already occurred and growth anticipated over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange for the Turnpike is also still in the design phase. The Midway Road Widening Project will add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: West Palm Beach evaluates elevated autonomous transit system linking airport to downtown
cards.teaser: Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, is proposing an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The system could cut the trip to less than 10 minutes.
cards.body:
Glydways, a California-based autonomous transit company, will present a proposal to Palm Beach County commissioners Tuesday for an elevated network of self-driving vehicles connecting downtown West Palm Beach to President Donald J. Trump International Airport. The system would also link to the convention center, Brightline and Tri-Rail stations. The company describes the concept as a modern alternative to traditional transit such as light rail, streetcars and people movers. Senior Vice President Brian Gettinger said the system functions like a "horizontal elevator," carrying passengers directly between destinations without getting stuck in traffic or making multiple intermediate stops. Small autonomous electric vehicles carrying about four to six passengers would travel along a dedicated elevated guideway built above existing roads, potentially cutting the trip between downtown and the airport to less than 10 minutes. Glydways estimates travel times of seven minutes or less between the convention center and airport and roughly one to two minutes between Tri-Rail and the convention center.

While Glydways has not disclosed a specific price tag, Gettinger said the system would cost "a small fraction" of a traditional light rail system while offering comparable passenger capacity. He referenced previous South Florida light rail discussions that carried estimates of $400 million to $500 million per mile. Funding could potentially come from Palm Beach County, the City of West Palm Beach, the Florida Department of Transportation, federal transit grants and public-private partnerships. Tuesday's County Commission meeting is not expected to approve construction, but rather determine whether the county should formally evaluate the proposal. If commissioners move forward, the county could seek competing bids and begin discussions on routes, station locations, costs and financing.

hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, and was the only Florida city selected for the honor this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has earned one of the nation's most prestigious civic honors, becoming the only Florida community selected as a 2026 All-America City Award winner. The National Civic League selected Riviera Beach as one of just 10 U.S. communities receiving the award this year. The recognition was announced at the National Civic League conference in Denver, where city leaders presented their community engagement initiatives to judges. Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the achievement, stating that "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." The award recognizes communities that effectively bring together residents, government agencies, businesses and organizations to address local challenges and create meaningful progress.

Lawson attributed the award to the city's long-term commitment to revitalization and improving quality of life for residents. "They're seeing the changes; they're seeing the revitalization and the reimagining of Riviera Beach that we set out so many years to do," he said. City leaders emphasized that the recognition reflects extensive efforts to strengthen civic health, build trust between residents and government, and empower community members to shape the city's future. The achievement comes after years of focused work on these priorities.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted three key programs that demonstrate its commitment to civic participation and neighborhood investment. The Riviera Beach Youth Council engages high school students in civic leadership and advocacy. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative, achieved a 98% completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program provides mini-grants to longtime homeowners for critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson emphasized that these efforts represent a broader partnership approach involving government, residents, faith organizations, schools and community groups. She stated that "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents. Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

Miller-Anderson noted that the award reinforces positive momentum and community pride in Riviera Beach's progress. City officials view the All-America City designation, presented annually since 1949, as validation that collaboration and resident involvement drive results in the community. The award signals to the nation that Riviera Beach is positioned for future growth and opportunities. Along with Riviera Beach, the 2026 honorees include Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road widening and new Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is moving forward with a $95 million Midway Road Widening Project and plans for a partial interchange at Florida's Turnpike. Last month, the City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the interchange addresses a significant gap between Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. "This is a way for us to try to accommodate the growth that's already occurred, but also the growth that will occur over the next 20 to 50 years," Samples said.

FDOT is currently constructing the first phase of the project, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, both currently in the design phase. The project will include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. The City Council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire, community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her and her fiancé Mark's Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, said she learned of the death through a phone call from Mark. "We received a call from Mark stating that Misty had passed away in a fire," Fenn said.

Fenn reflected on White's character and how she wants her to be remembered. "Misty was a Christian woman. She loved gardening and plants. She plays the piano," Fenn said, noting that White was always the first to lend a hand and loved kids and people. The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak, as Misty's birthday is the Fourth of July and she passed just days before it. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, having lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the fire destroyed many of his and White's belongings. "It's completely a state of devastation," Fenn said.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year, ground beef and buns up most
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition is becoming more expensive this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. Inflation is driving the price increases across multiple cookout staples. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, while buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, damaged by a Florida frost, have seen the steepest increase at 12.4%. Ice cream prices have also climbed 5.3% compared to last year.

Not all cookout items have become more expensive. Potato prices are down this year, offering savings for families planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends families shop strategically to manage costs. "It's really important to shop savvier than ever, it is comparing the stores to see who has the best deals for the groceries on your list," Woroch said. She emphasized that cutting down food waste is crucial for families, which begins with making a meal plan.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied coverage for reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance company Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield deny coverage for a reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy. Less than 24 hours before her scheduled reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involving GalaFlex, a synthetic surgical mesh, was deemed "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body and popular among plastic surgeons, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label, experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the treatment's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and contends the product produces fewer complications than other options. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the mesh more than a week ago. Last year, following investigative reporting that shared breast cancer patients' denial stories, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem stated the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial while a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is challenging a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009, who was suspended following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in her recommendation, stating that "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney contends that Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk was a "serious offense" and that his removal was appropriate.

Theobald's comments labeled Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. Administrative Law Judge Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge also recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald will be reinstated.

hero.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
hero.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football program is focused on winning a state championship as they prepare for the upcoming 2026 fall season. Last year, the team finished with a 10-2 record and won their district title, but their playoff run ended in disappointment when they lost in the second round. That early exit has motivated the program to aim higher this year.

Head coach Jimmy Robertson emphasized that the team has a strong foundation built on continuity. Most of the current seniors have been with the program for four years, and many came up through the middle school program. This veteran leadership has brought success throughout their high school careers, and Robertson believes this senior class has the potential to deliver the best season in program history. The coaching staff is confident that experienced players who understand how the program operates can push the team to new heights.

To prepare for deeper playoff runs, the Scots have intentionally scheduled more challenging opponents this fall. Senior Jack Williams explained that the team wanted to elevate their program by competing against top-tier teams. Playing stronger competition serves two purposes: it tests their abilities and helps attract talented players to the program. Senior Jack Whelche stressed that success this season will not be measured by regular season performance alone. He noted that an undefeated regular season means nothing if the team continues to lose in the second round of playoffs. The goal is simply to advance further than they did last year and make a real playoff push.

The players are using their summer training sessions as fuel for the upcoming season. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily grind of workouts provides motivation and something to work toward. Each training session adds up as the team builds toward their goals. The Scots are using their preparation and hard work as a foundation to break their previous records and finish the season with positive results. With their experienced senior class, more demanding schedule, and clear focus on playoff success, Saint Andrew's believes they have the pieces in place to make a state title run this fall.

Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices before heading out. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said of the holiday celebrations.

cards.headline: Lantana veteran gets lien removed and roof fixed after WPTV investigation
cards.teaser: Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, had a nearly $7,000 lien lifted from his home and unfinished roof repairs completed after WPTV contacted the roofing contractor.
cards.body:
Stephen McCoy, a disabled and retired veteran in Lantana, hired Seabreeze Roofing and Sheet Metal in Boynton Beach to replace his nearly 20-year-old roof ahead of hurricane season. McCoy made six payments to the company totaling more than $17,000. He said he was mostly satisfied with the work except for two holes left unfinished on the back side of his home. When McCoy tried to get the company to finish the repairs, he said they stopped responding. Between January 10 and February 5, McCoy called, texted and emailed the company multiple times without success.

Letters from Gulfeagle Supply then arrived at McCoy's home warning that the company had filed a nearly $7,000 lien with the county. The lien document stated that Gulfeagle Supply had furnished materials to Seabreeze Roofing for McCoy's property but was not paid. McCoy turned to WPTV investigative reporter Kate Hussey for help. After Hussey spoke with the owner of Seabreeze Roofing, who declined to comment on camera, she returned to McCoy's home within an hour with a final waiver of lien signed by Gulfeagle Supply and notarized, lifting the lien from his home. About an hour later, McCoy sent WPTV a photo of crews back on his roof finishing the job.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with a partial interchange on the Turnpike.
cards.body:
The Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to donate 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, noted there is a significant gap between the current entrances and exits to the Turnpike in the city. Samples explained the interchange addresses accessibility and accommodates growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety. The first phase widens the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road, currently under construction. The second phase, from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road, remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, both still in design phases. The project will include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. City council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient denied reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was denied insurance coverage for breast reconstruction surgery less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. Her insurance company cited the surgical mesh as investigational.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, the most common type of breast cancer. She decided on a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction to eliminate any possibility of recurrence. Clark had the mastectomy, but less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure involving a surgical mesh called GalaFlex.

According to her denial letter, the surgery is still considered "investigational" and "there is no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is a synthetic surgical mesh approved by the FDA for some uses in the body but not approved for breast reconstruction and is still considered an off-label, investigational and experimental treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA reiterated its stance that the efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined. Despite the denial, Clark got her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after her plastic surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, found a mechanism to make it happen. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Clark and Billington are still fighting the denial.

hero.headline: North Palm Beach Celebrates Fourth of July with Fireworks and America 250 Events
hero.teaser: North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4.
hero.body:
The free community event includes a pool party, lawn games, live music, a barbecue buffet and a fireworks finale scheduled for 9 p.m. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The festivities begin with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach Offers Sea Turtle Nesting Programs Through September
cards.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots, and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. According to the center, these programs are designed to give visitors an opportunity to learn more about sea turtle conservation along one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation, and ongoing research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include the use of red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes, and research tag scanning equipment. Loggerhead Marinelife Center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data related to nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups encourage beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash, and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

hero.headline: Secretary of State Cord Byrd Seeks to Block Paula Stark From House District 47 Ballot After Filing Failure
hero.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking a Leon Circuit Court to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork before the June 12 qualifying deadline. Stark filed her qualifying materials less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline, which state officials say prevented her from discovering a critical missing document. Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests required for all candidates, was never submitted by her treasurer and partner, Joel Davis.

Five state employees provided sworn written declarations stating that Davis never submitted Form 6 and was not accidentally handed it back when he submitted other paperwork during the final hour of the qualifying window. Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said in a court filing that three weeks after the deadline, Stark still has not submitted Form 6. According to Reeve, Stark was one of 12 candidates who failed to properly turn in the form, though half of them corrected the problems and qualified. Byrd argued that Stark and Davis knew Form 6 was required and could have discovered the missing document if they had not waited until the final hour to file their materials.

Reeve also documented a pattern of filing problems with Stark's campaign. The campaign has filed finance reports more than a month late, reported excessive contributions, and maintained an incorrect address on file. Audits in 2022 and 2024 found inconsistent transfers between campaign and office accounts. Additionally, a late report fine upheld by the Florida Elections Commission was referred to debt collection for nonpayment in November 2025. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November due to over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines.

If Stark remains off the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 would be open to all voters to decide between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves. No other Republicans filed to run in the traditionally blue House District representing Osceola and Orange counties. Byrd emphasized the time constraints involved in the decision, noting that ballots must be mailed to overseas military and their families by July 4, with vote-by-mail ballots due out between July 9 and 16. The Secretary of State argued that reversing course would be costly and likely risk confusion in the results of this race and others on the ballot.

cards.headline: DeSantis Allies Accuse Lieutenant Governor's Wife of Running Burner Accounts Critical of Governor
cards.teaser: Multiple social media accounts were deactivated after prominent veterans of Governor Ron DeSantis' communications team alleged they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins.
cards.body:
Multiple X accounts were suddenly deactivated after allegations emerged that they were tied to Layla Collins, wife of Lieutenant Governor Jay Collins. Christina Pushaw, a communications specialist in the Governor's Office, and Jeremy Redfern, Deputy Chief of Staff to Attorney General James Uthmeier, both pointed to online research connecting the accounts to the Second Lady. Pushaw shared information posted by Promota CEO Robert Salvador showing that the account @FSUdude01670 appeared connected to a phone number similar to a known number and email used by Layla Collins. Florida Politics obtained screenshots verifying this through two-factor authentication. Pushaw also identified a second account, @bobnamy1, that she said appeared tied to Layla Collins.

Pushaw said the content of the accounts suggested they existed entirely to advance Jay Collins' political ambitions as he runs for Governor. Redfern confirmed the FSUdude account was tied directly to her personal cell phone number. Both accounts were deactivated after Pushaw and Redfern leveled their criticisms publicly. Both Pushaw and Redfern previously served as Press Secretaries for DeSantis. Redfern now works for Uthmeier, who has endorsed U.S. Representative Byron Donalds for Governor. DeSantis appointed Jay Collins as Lieutenant Governor last year but has declined to endorse a preferred successor in the Governor's race. DeSantis cannot seek a third term because of term limits.

cards.headline: St. Petersburg Selects $8.1 Billion Proposal to Redevelop Tropicana Field Site Around Civic Park and Museum
cards.teaser: St. Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch selected The Burg Bid as the city's preferred proposal for redeveloping Tropicana Field and the Historic Gas Plant District, centered on a 13-acre civic park and permanent home for The Woodson African American Museum of Florida.
cards.body:
Led by Blake Investment Partners and Related Group, The Burg Bid calls for purchasing 58 acres of city-owned land for $275 million, with the full land package valued at $405 million when factoring in $130 million in land the city would retain. The proposal would be organized around Samuel Davis Park, a 13-acre central park meant to become a civic and cultural space for the district. The park would be part of 18.5 acres of public park space and would include The Woodson African American Museum of Florida, a Museum of Public Art, a Discovery Center, event lawns, a playground, a splash pad, café areas, public art and a concert lawn. The proposal also includes plans for a surf wave attraction, recreation deck, multimodal hub, workforce and small-business center, and Resilience Event Center.

The plan calls for 3,600 income-restricted housing units over a 15-year buildout, with 1,800 units planned within the Historic Gas Plant District and another 1,800 on complementary sites elsewhere in St. Petersburg. The district would be built in three main phases, each expected to take about five years. Phase 1 would establish the district's cultural and workforce anchors, including The Woodson, the Collaboratorium workforce training and small-business center, the Legacy Link pedestrian corridor and a multimodal transportation hub. The proposal also calls for restoring Booker Creek, which was reduced to a drainage ditch between parking lots and Tropicana Field. The Rays' lease with the city ends after the 2028 season.

hero.headline: Hobe Sound woman killed in home fire days before her birthday
hero.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday in a fire at her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
hero.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday when a fire engulfed her Hobe Sound home. The sheriff's office has identified a possible electrical issue as the cause, though the investigation remains ongoing. White's fiancé, Mark, was also in the home at the time of the fire. Friends and family are now rallying around him as he faces the loss of his fiancée and the destruction of their belongings.

Nina Fenn, who had been friends with White for eight years, learned of the tragedy through a phone call from Mark. Fenn visited the scene in the days following the fire to process her grief. "It's just a terrible shame and awful loss of life," Fenn said. She reflected on White's character and the impact she had on those around her. According to Fenn, White was a Christian woman who enjoyed gardening and plants and played the piano. "She was always the first to lend a hand," Fenn said. "She loves kids; she loves her kids. She loves people."

The tragedy carries additional weight for Mark, who has already endured significant personal loss. Mark previously lost his only child, Jacob, in what Fenn described as a tragic circumstance. "Mark lost his one and only child, Jacob, and lost him tragically. So, I just am trying whatever I can to support him," Fenn said. The community has launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild his life after the fire destroyed much of what he and White owned together.

The timing of White's death adds another layer of heartbreak to an already devastating situation. White's birthday was July 4, meaning she passed away just days before turning another year older. Those who knew her say her memory will endure in their hearts. "She's always been a good soul to me. She'll always be in our hearts," Fenn said. As the investigation into the fire's cause continues, the community continues to support Mark during this difficult time.

Deputies reported the discovery following a search operation in the area. The incident marks a recovery effort along the St. Lucie County coastline.

cards.headline: Two people rescued after boat sinks in Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County
cards.teaser: Two people were rescued after their boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County on Thursday.
cards.body:
Two people were rescued after their boat sank in the Intracoastal Waterway in St. Lucie County. The incident occurred on Thursday and was captured on bodycam footage.

Rescue crews responded to the scene and successfully pulled both individuals from the water. The boat went down in the Intracoastal Waterway, a major waterway in St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce man arrested on child pornography charges
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce man was arrested on child pornography charges, according to the sheriff's office.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce man was arrested on child pornography charges, the sheriff's office said. The arrest was announced on Thursday.

The sheriff's office reported the charges against the Fort Pierce resident. The case involves allegations of possession of child pornography materials.

cards.headline: Costco plans first Treasure Coast store in Port St. Lucie
cards.teaser: Costco is planning to open its first Treasure Coast location in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Costco is moving forward with plans to open its first store on the Treasure Coast in Port St. Lucie. The warehouse retailer announced the location for the new store on Friday.

The Port St. Lucie location will mark the first Costco presence in the Treasure Coast region. The store will bring the wholesale club's membership-based shopping model to St. Lucie County residents.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward on Midway Road widening and new Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie is advancing a major infrastructure project to widen Midway Road and add a partial interchange to Florida's Turnpike. Last month, the Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation to assist with the interchange. The city council will vote on final approval to give the land at an upcoming meeting. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said there is a significant gap between entrances and exits to the Turnpike currently in Port St. Lucie. The interchange addresses accessibility and aims to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT has been constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to help with congestion and safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes from Selvitz Road to Jenkins Road. The second widening phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road is still in the design phase, with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. The partial interchange is also still in the design phase. FDOT said the Midway Road Widening Project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks.

cards.headline: Legacy Lions Football team standings updated for Port St. Lucie school
cards.teaser: The Legacy Lions Football team in Port St. Lucie has updated standings for the current season.
cards.body:
Legacy Lions Football team standings for Port St. Lucie were updated on Friday. The team represents a Port St. Lucie high school in local football competition.

The standings update provides current information on the Legacy Lions' performance this season. The team competes in high school football in St. Lucie County.

hero.headline: Indian River State College Promise Program offers debt-free college degrees
hero.teaser: Indian River State College is helping students achieve college degrees without taking on debt through its Promise Program.
hero.body:
Indian River State College operates a Promise Program designed to help students earn college degrees without accumulating debt. The program provides financial assistance to qualifying students across the college's service area.

The Promise Program addresses the rising cost of higher education by covering expenses that would otherwise require students to take out loans. Indian River State College serves students across the Treasure Coast region.

The program reflects a growing trend among community colleges to remove financial barriers to higher education. Students who complete the Promise Program graduate with degrees and no student loan debt.

cards.headline: Vero Beach buries community time capsule to be opened in 2076
cards.teaser: Vero Beach residents gathered Friday to bury a community-wide time capsule that will remain sealed for 50 years.
cards.body:
Vero Beach residents gathered Friday to bury a community-wide time capsule that will remain sealed for 50 years. The capsule is scheduled to be opened in 2076.

The time capsule represents a snapshot of life in Vero Beach in 2026. Residents contributed items and memories to be preserved for future generations to discover half a century from now.

The burial took place Friday in Vero Beach. The capsule will serve as a link between current residents and those who will live in the community five decades in the future.

The opening date of 2076 will mark the 100th anniversary of the United States bicentennial and the 150th anniversary of this time capsule project. Future Vero Beach residents will have the opportunity to see what life was like in their community during the summer of 2026.

cards.headline: 9896 Pine St listed for sale in Sebastian
cards.teaser: A property at 9896 Pine St in Sebastian is now on the real estate market.
cards.body:
The home at 9896 Pine St in Sebastian, FL 32976 has been listed for sale. The property appeared on Realtor.com Friday.

The Sebastian property is located in Indian River County. The listing provides an opportunity for buyers interested in the Sebastian residential market.

Potential buyers can find additional details about the property through Realtor.com and local real estate agents serving the Sebastian area.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% from last year
cards.teaser: Families celebrating Independence Day with cookouts will pay more this year as food prices continue to rise.
cards.body:
A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey. Ground beef prices rose 5.5%, while buns increased 7.7%. Strawberries experienced the steepest increase at 12.4%, driven by damage from a Florida frost. Ice cream prices climbed 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples became more expensive. Potato prices dropped this year, offering relief for potato chip and salad shoppers. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can offer better deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommended comparing stores for the best deals and reducing food waste through meal planning as ways to keep costs in check.

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band will march down the National Mall on July 4, representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade, representing the entire state of Florida. On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the students will march a full mile along the National Mall, from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event.

Junior Lola Cabezas said millions, if not billions, of people will be watching the parade. She noted that marching band is more physically demanding than most people realize, requiring students to play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound. Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is laser-focused on nailing every detail, with everyone able to see what the Boca High band is capable of. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone expressed full confidence in her students as they head into the national spotlight. Senior Lily Schaffer said making it to D.C. proves how far the program has grown and showcases what the program does. The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those who want to watch from home.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season 10-2 with a district championship and are preparing for a deeper playoff run this fall.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team finished the 2025 season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit has motivated them to aim higher for 2026. Head coach Jimmy Robertson noted that most of the seniors are four-year players who came up through the middle school program and have experienced success throughout their careers. "Most of these seniors are four-year seniors. I mean, if not the majority of them came from the middle school as well. So they know how things are run," Robertson said.

To compete at a higher level, the Scots have scheduled more challenging opponents for the upcoming fall season. Senior Jack Williams explained the reasoning behind the tougher schedule: "We knew that we wanted to take our program to the next level. So we really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete." Senior Jack Whelche emphasized that the team's definition of improvement goes beyond a strong regular season. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. Obviously we wanna go undefeated in the season, but that doesn't matter if we keep losing in the second round of the playoffs," Whelche said. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the demanding summer workouts serve as motivation for achieving those goals.

cards.headline: Florida school districts earn A ratings from state education department
cards.teaser: School districts across Florida received letter grades from the state, with several earning top marks for student performance.
cards.body:
The Florida Department of Education released annual school district ratings based on student performance on state tests, graduation rates, and advanced coursework participation. School districts and individual schools receive letter grades ranging from A to F.

The ratings reflect student achievement across all grade levels and measure participation in Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge AICE, and Dual Enrollment courses. Districts use the ratings to track progress and identify areas for improvement.

The state education department evaluates schools and districts each year using a points-based system tied to standardized test scores and other academic indicators. The 2026 ratings were released Friday.
